labels.note: Removing early return changes output for query/fragment-only inputs, e.g. '#foo' becomes '/#foo' instead of '#foo'.
Only differs when query string contains a literal extra '?', an unusual/malformed input; corrupts reconstructed query.
Same as withoutTrailingSlash case: only affects rare inputs with literal '?' inside query value.
Removing the '?' check makes withBase duplicate the base for any input already ending base+'?query', a common case.
nextChar==='' is already covered by the preceding !nextChar check, so this branch is unreachable/redundant.
Skips the empty-base short-circuit; changes output for inputs like '//evil.com' with empty base (protocol-relative edge case).
Same effect as disabling the isEmptyURL check: falls through to slash-collapsing logic, altering output for empty/'/' base.
Unanchored regex can strip a '//' occurring later in the string (e.g. inside query value) instead of only leading slashes.
